payloads.description:
The Rodent Research-3 (RR-3) mission was sponsored by the pharmaceutical company Eli Lilly and Co. and the Center for the Advancement of Science in Space to study the effectiveness of a potential countermeasure for the loss of muscle and bone mass that occurs during spaceflight. Twenty BALB/c, 12-weeks old female mice (ten controls and ten treated) were flown to the ISS and housed in the Rodent Habitat for 39-42 days. Twenty mice of similar age, sex and strain were used for ground controls housed in identical hardware and matching ISS environmental conditions. Basal controls were housed in standard vivarium cages. Spaceflight, ground controls and basal groups had blood collected, then were euthanized, had one hind limb removed, and finally whole carcasses were stored at -80 C until dissection. All mice in this data set received only the control/sham injection. Microdissection of retinae from previously frozen eyes and RNA isolation were performed in the laboratory of Dr. Xiao Mao at Loma Linda University.

The goal was to evaluate a potential new treatment for skeletal muscle wasting and weakness. Working with NASA, the researchers assessed its ability to prevent these conditions in mice exposed to long-duration spaceflight. Rodent research models have made it possible to study serious diseases involving muscle atrophy, and even age-related weakness. Conducting this study during spaceflight provided the researchers with the rare opportunity to expose all the muscles of an organism to conditions that will produce atrophy – something not easily achieved on Earth.

The mission objectives

Although the primary research focus of Rodent Research-3 is skeletal muscle, the investigators were studying other organ systems, such as bone, both at the tissue and molecular levels. Their goal is to characterize tissue responses to spaceflight and observe how these changes vary with the length of time spent in microgravity. The findings will advance our understanding of the risks that long-term space exploration poses to astronauts and can be applied towards the development of countermeasures to protect astronaut health. 


IACUC Protocol Number:  CAS-15-001-Y1

All animal procedures performed in these experiments were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and use Committees (IACUC) numbers NASA: CAS-15-001-Y1 for flight at the NASA Ames Research Center (ARC) and the Kennedy Space Center (KSC) and the methods were carried out in accordance with relevant guidelines and regulations.


NASA Space Biology Biospecimen Sharing Program (BSP) Activities

The NASA Space Biology Biospecimen Sharing Program collected biospecimens from RR-3 to maximize the scientific return from the biological spaceflight.  Portion of the Rodent Research 3 data collection contains environmental and acceleration data pertain to the SpaceX CRS-8 Dragon vehicle as it carried the Rodent Research payload to the International Space Station.  Another portion of the Rodent Research 3 data collection contains environmental monitoring data for the Rodent Research experiment on the International Space Station (ISS), and in associated ground controls at Kennedy Space Center.  RR3 Basal controls Dissection performed in Colorado 9/12-16/16. BSP tissues collected from the 10 non-treated control group and shipped to ALSDA.

protocols.description: A cohort of 12-week-old female BALB/c mice were flown to the ISS and housed in the Rodent Habitat and were subjected to microgravity for 39-42 days. Mice of similar age, sex and strain were used for ground controls housed in identical hardware and matching ISS environmental conditions. mice from the same cohort were dissected at time of launch and used as basal controls.  At the end of the mission, spaceflight and ground controls had blood collected, were euthanized and one hindlimb removed and whole carcasses were stored at -80 C until BSP (Biospecimen Sharing Program) dissection on earth. The study followed recommendations in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and the protocol was approved by the NASA Flight Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC). [Spaceflight and ground control mice- untreated, injected with control Ig-G (sham treated). Basal mice received no injections.]
protocols.name: animal husbandry

protocols.description: Mouse carcasses were removed from -80 C storage and thawed at room temperature for 15-20 minutes for dissection. Each carcass dissection time was no longer than 1 hour from collection of the first tissue. Multiple tissues, including the eye tissue, were collected from each carcass. Eye tissues were harvested and snap frozen in LN2, then stored separately in -80 C freezer for sample processing.  Frozen whole eye samples were sent to Dr. Vivien (Xiao) Mao at Loma Linda University for microdissection and RNA extraction.  Frozen whole eye samples were microdissected in ice-cold PBS.  Fine spring scissors were used to separate the cornea from the sclera to access the retina. The retina was carefully detached from the sclera. The retina, cornea, and lens were immediately frozen on dry ice and stored at -80 C until DNA/RNA isolation.
protocols.name: sample collection

protocols.description: The absorbed dose of ionizing radiation received by biological payloads on the International Space Station (ISS) depends on a number of factors, including date and duration of exposure and location of the payload on the ISS. Some of the factors that lead to variations in the absorbed dose rate in orbit are ISS altitude, period during the solar cycle, and location of the sample—the ISS module and the specific location within that module. Shielding effects from the biological payload container or habitat have not been taken into account. The measured absorbed dose can vary based on the dosimetry instrument(s) used. Radiation monitoring on the ISS is not standardized across modules; each international partner has its own suite of instruments, with differing technologies, sensitivities and analysis methodologies, including criteria for distinguishing between lightly ionizing particles (mainly protons) and highly ionizing particles (mainly galactic cosmic ray nuclei). Both active and passive dosimeters are used. Active dosimeters are powered and data are read out and stored and/or telemetered to ground. Some active dosimeters provide additional levels of detail such as time resolution, energy deposition and particle identification. Passive dosimeters are unpowered, record constantly and are read out upon return to the ground. The dose in the metadata is the dose recorded by the radiation detector closest to the sample. In most cases that detector will be in the same ISS module; in cases where data from a detector in the same module are not available, the dose is extrapolated using data from periods where data are available from detectors in multiple modules, including the module containing the payload. The duration of the experiment is defined as the time in space during which the specimen was “living”, including the time on the delivery vehicle (e.g. SpaceX Dragon). Once the specimen was frozen or fixed, the experiment was considered stopped. Details of ISS dosimetry and a table with doses for all GeneLab ISS experiment ISS datasets are available at https://genelab.nasa.gov/environmental/radiation.
protocols.name: radiation dosimetry

protocols.description: RNA was extracted using the AllPrep DNA/RNA/miRNA Universal Kit (Qiagen, Cat # 80224) by Loma Linda University. Frozen retinal tissues were homogenized in 600 ul of RLT lysis buffer containing 1 % beta-mercaptoethanol.  Tissue homogenization was performed using tissue homogenizing bead mix (Tissue homogenizing CKMix, Precellys) on Minilys (Bertin Technologies).  Tubes were centrifuged for 1 min at 20, 000 g to reduce bubbles/foam.  The homogenized lysate was transferred to an AllPrep DNA Mini spin column placed in a 2 ml collection tube and centrifuged for 30 s at full speed (maximum speed of 20,000 x g).  The flow-through (containing the RNA) was transferred into a new 2 ml microcentrifuge for RNA purification. The AllPrep DNA Mini spin column (containing the DNA) was stored on ice for DNA purification.  80 ul Proteinase K was added to the flow-through (RNA) and mixed by pipetting.  350 ul of 100 % Ethanol was added and mixed and incubated for 10 minutes at room temperature.  750 ul 100% ethanol was added and mixed.  700 ul of the sample was transferred to an RNeasy Mini spin column placed in a 2 ml collection tube and centrifuged for 15 s at 20,000 x g. This step was repeated until the entire sample passed through the column. The flow-through was discarded.  500 ul of Buffer RPE was added to the RNeasy Mini spin column, centrifuged for 15 s at full speed (20,000 x g) and the flow-through discarded.  10 u DNase I stock solution was diluted in 70 ul Buffer RDD mixed gently and the 80 ul incubation mix was added to the spin column and kept for 15 minutes at room temperature.  500 ul Buffer FRN was added to the RNeasy Mini spin column and centrifuged for 15 s at 20,000 x g.  The flow-through (containing small RNAS) was re-applied to the spin column and centrifuged.  The flow-through was then discarded.  500 ul Buffer RPE was then added to the RNeasy Mini spin column and centrifuged for 15 s at 20,000 x g.  500 ul of 100% ethanol was added to the RNeasy Mini spin column and centrifuged for 2 min at 20,000 x g.  The flow-through and the collection tube were discarded.  Centrifugation was repeated with new collection tubes.  The RNeasy Mini spin column was placed in a new 1.5 ml collection tube and 30 ul RNase-free water was added directly to the spin column membrane and centrifuged for 1 min at 10000 x g to elute the RNA.  The eluate was re-applied to the column and centrifuged again to increase the RNA yield from the column.  RNA concentration was measured using Qubit Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA).  RNA quality was assessed using the Agilent 4200 TapeStation with the Agilent RNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA).  RNA stored at -80 C.

protocols.description: Frozen RNA aliquot was kept on dry ice for control addition.  ERCC ExFold RNA Spike-In Mixes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA Cat # 4456739) at 1:100 dilution of either Mix 1 or Mix 2 were added to the sample tube at the concentrations suggested by the manufacturer protocol.  Samples were shipped on dry ice to omics core facility.

protocols.description: Raw fastq files from each sample were assessed for % rRNA using HTStream SeqScreener (version 1.0.0) screened against a fasta file of Mus musculus rRNA sequences retrieved from NCBI on 01-June-2019. Raw fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1) and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports.
protocols.name: GeneLab raw data processing protocol

protocols.description: Data were processed as described in GL-DPPD-7101-G (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/master/RNAseq/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7101_Versions/GL-DPPD-7101-G.md), using NF_RCP version 2.1.0 (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_RNASeq_Workflow/tree/NF_RCP_2.1.0). In short, raw fastq files were filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10) powered by Cutadapt (version 4.2). Trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Mus Musculus STAR and RSEM references were built using STAR (version 2.7.11b) and RSEM (version 1.3.3), respectively, Ensembl release 112, genome assembly GRCm39 (Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa) concatenated with ERCC92.fa from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip), and the following gtf annotation file: Mus_musculus.GRCm39.112.gtf concatenated with the ERCC92.gtf file from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip). Trimmed reads were aligned to the Mus Musculus + ERCC STAR reference with STAR (version 2.7.11b) and alignment log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). Aligned reads were assessed for strandedness using RSeQC infer_experiment.py (version 5.0.4), gene body coverage using RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py (version 5.0.4), inner distance was assessed using RSeQC inner_distance.py (version 5.0.4), and distribution of RNA features using RSeQC read_distribution.py (version 5.0.4). Aligned reads from all samples were quantified using RSEM (version 1.3.3), with strandedness set to reverse and RSEM count log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). To create a set of rRNA-removed quantification data, Ensembl IDs mapping to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) were removed from the RSEM gene count data. Both the original set of RSEM quantification data and the rRNA-removed data were subject to differential gene expression analysis as follows. A runsheet was generated with dp_tools (version 1.3.8) and the runsheet and quantification data were imported to R (version 4.4.2) with tximport (version 1.34.0), ERCC genes were removed, and the non-ERCC genes were normalized with DESeq2 (version 1.46.0) median of ratios method. Normalized gene counts were subject to differential expression analysis. Differential expression analysis was performed in R (version 4.4.2) using DESeq2 (version 1.46.0); all groups were compared pairwise using the Wald test and the likelihood ratio test was used to generate the F statistic p-value. Gene annotations were assigned using the custom annotation tables generated in-house as detailed in GL-DPPD-7110-A (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/GL_RefAnnotTable-A_1.1.0/GeneLab_Reference_Annotations/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7110_Versions/GL-DPPD-7110-A/GL-DPPD-7110-A.md), with STRINGdb (version 2.16.4), PANTHER.db (version 1.0.12), and org.Mm.eg.db (version 3.19.1). Assessment of ERCC spiked genes was performed as detailed in the ERCC_analysis_GLbulkRNAseq.html report.
